questions.q: This page treats membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis and mesangiocapillary glomerulonephritis as names for the same entity.
opts: False — the two are separated by which complement pathway is involved
True — and the page notes that the entity is common in children
True — the eponym line reads 'a.k.a. mesangiocapillary glomerulonephritis' for MPGN
False — mesangiocapillary GN is the older term for IgA nephropathy
questions.exp: a.k.a mesangiocapillary glomerulonephritis; rare disease. (Book p770)

questions.q: Match each MPGN column with its feature — 1) Type I immunofluorescence (capillary wall & mesangium) 2) Type II immunofluorescence 3) Type II outcome post transplant … A) 100% recurrence B) C3 ± IgG/M C) IgG + IgM ± C3
questions.exp: Type I IF: IgG + IgM ± C3; Type II (C3 GN): C3 ± IgG/M; Type II post transplant: 100% recurrence. (Book p770)

questions.q: C3 glomerulonephritis is the label this page attaches to type II MPGN.
opts: True — type II is labelled C3 GN
False — C3 GN is the label written against type I MPGN
False — the page prints C4 GN beside type II MPGN
True — and the same label is applied to post-infectious GN
questions.exp: Type II: C3 GN. (Book p770)

questions.q: Outcome post transplant in the classification table: Type I recurs in 80% of cases while Type II recurs in:
questions.exp: Type I 80% recurrence; Type II 100% recurrence. (Book p770)

questions.q: A resident wants to know whether a search for systemic causes can be skipped in a biopsy-proven MPGN. The banner over the secondary-cause block of the table states:
opts: A fifth of cases, and only when an infection is found
All (100%), as the banner of that block reads
Only the type I subset, which is about half of cases
None — MPGN is always treated as a primary disease
questions.exp: Secondary causes (100% cases are secondary to systemic causes). (Book p770)

questions.q: The monoclonal (malignancies) row of MPGN secondary causes lists plasma cell dyscrasias and:
opts: Multiple myeloma as the only listed entity
Acute myeloid leukemia with circulating blasts
questions.exp: Monoclonal: plasma cell dyscrasias; chronic lymphoid leukemia (CLL). (Book p770)

questions.q: A child returns from a malarious region with nephritic features and low C3; the infection line of the type I table is read. Which organisms and diseases appear on that line?
opts: HIV and parvovirus B19, the pair listed under secondary FSGS
Hepatitis C, infective endocarditis, leprosy and P. malariae
Plasmodium falciparum with cerebral involvement, not quartan malaria
Hepatitis B with schistosomiasis, the pair seen in membranous disease
questions.exp: Infections: HCV, infective endocarditis, leprosy, Plasmodium malariae (Quartan malarial nephropathy). (Book p770)

questions.q: The shunt example and autoimmune trio under polyclonal Type I causes are:
questions.exp: Shunts: eg. ventriculoperitoneal shunt; autoimmune: SLE, Sjogren's, scleroderma. (Book p770)

questions.q: Type II MPGN's polyclonal associations are acquired partial lipodystrophy of face and:
questions.exp: Type II: acquired partial lipodystrophy of face; optic nerve drusen. (Book p770)

questions.q: Match each deposit feature with its MPGN type — 1) Type I EM appearance 2) Type I deposit location 3) Type II deposit location … A) Intramembranous + mesangial B) Train track/double contour appearance C) Subendothelial + mesangial
questions.exp: Type I: train track/double contour; subendothelial + mesangial. Type II: intramembranous + mesangial. (Book p770)

questions.q: Type II MPGN carries the eponym intramembranous dense deposit disease.
opts: False — the eponym printed for type II is type III MPGN
True — and both labels imply that complement studies are normal
True — intramembranous dense deposit disease is the eponym
False — dense deposit disease is the eponym reserved for type I MPGN
questions.exp: AKA intramembranous dense deposit disease. (Book p770)

questions.q: MPGN light-microscopy findings are thickening of capillary wall, mesangial > endocapillary proliferation/hypercellularity, and:
opts: Diffuse crescent formation filling Bowman's space
Spike and dome formation along the glomerular basement membrane
Lobular capillary tuft, sometimes with uniform nodules
questions.exp: Lobular appearance of capillary tuft ± nodules (multiple small uniform nodules). (Book p771)

questions.q: The MPGN photomicrograph is captioned mesangial proliferation, with the pointer labelling:
opts: Tubular microcysts of the collapsing pattern
Subepithelial spikes highlighted on silver stain
Accentuated lobular appearance of the capillary tuft
Crescent formation filling the urinary space
questions.exp: Figure label: accentuated lobular appearance of capillary duct; caption mesangial proliferation. (Book p771)

questions.q: The MPGN clinical-presentation split is 35% nephrotic, 35% nephritic, 20% CKD with contracted kidney and:
questions.exp: 35% nephrotic; 35% nephritic; 20% CKD with contracted kidney; 10% RPGN type 2. (Book p771)

questions.q: Match each MPGN presentation arm with its share — 1) Nephrotic syndrome 2) CKD with contracted kidney 3) RPGN type 2 … A) 10% B) 35% C) 20%
questions.exp: Nephrotic 35%; CKD with contracted kidney 20%; RPGN type 2 10%. (Book p771)

questions.q: MPGN prognosis is written as poor, with what proportion of cases heading to CKD?
questions.exp: Poor prognosis; 100% cases → CKD. (Book p771)

questions.q: The HCV extrahepatic manifestations note lists porphyria cutanea tarda, lichen planus, Sjogrens syndrome and:
questions.exp: HCV extrahepatic: porphyria cutanea tarda, lichen planus, Sjogrens syndrome, cryoglobulinemia. (Book p771)

questions.q: A hepatitis C patient with arthralgia develops palpable purpuric spots on both legs with a normal platelet count. The note on this page attributes the picture to:
opts: Cryoglobulinemia, one of the listed extrahepatic features
Porphyria cutanea tarda, the other cutaneous manifestation named
Hepatitis C-associated membranous nephropathy with subepithelial deposits
Thrombocytopenic purpura from the underlying liver disease
questions.exp: Cryoglobulinemia → non thrombocytopenic palpable purpura. (Book p771)

questions.q: Fill up: IgA nephropathy (Berger's disease, Henoch-Schonlein nephritis) carries the tag of being the ______ glomerular disease.
questions.exp: AKA Henoch-Schonlein nephritis/Berger's disease; m/c glomerular disease. (Book p771)

questions.q: Match each IgA fact with its type — 1) mIgA (monomeric) production site 2) pIgA (polymeric) production site 3) pIgA normal clearance organ … A) Liver B) Bone marrow C) MALT (mucosa associated lymphoid tissue)
questions.exp: mIgA produced in bone marrow; pIgA produced in MALT; normally cleared by liver. (Book p771)

questions.q: Which IgA-type statement is TRUE as per the etiopathogenesis tree?
opts: Monomeric IgA is produced in the mucosa
Polymeric IgA is produced in bone marrow
Monomeric IgA is normally cleared by the kidney
Polymeric IgA is made in MALT and cleared by the liver
questions.exp: mIgA (monomeric): bone marrow; pIgA (polymeric): MALT, normally cleared by liver. (Book p771)

questions.q: The mucosal-injury causes of secondary IgA nephropathy include all of these EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Mucosal injury: coeliac, Whipple, tropical sprue, Crohns, ulcerative colitis, HIV. (Book p772)

questions.q: HIV sits in the mucosal-injury list, but its m/c associated glomerular lesion is:
questions.exp: HIV (m/c collapsing FSGS) in the mucosal injury list; the liver-disease table pairs HIV with collapsing FSGS. (Book p772)

questions.q: Cirrhosis appears as a secondary cause of IgA nephropathy because the damaged liver cannot clear immune complexes.
opts: True — and the identical reason is printed against hepatitis B
True — the bracket reads 'liver cannot clear immune complex'
False — the bracket reads 'liver overproduces IgA'
False — cirrhosis is listed because portal hypertension damages glomeruli
questions.exp: Cirrhosis: (liver cannot clear immune complex). (Book p772)

questions.q: The spondyloarthritis examples in adults are ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, reactive arthritis and IBD-associated arthritis, where the book ranks:
questions.exp: IBD associated arthritis (CD > UC). (Book p772)

questions.q: In the innocent bystander mechanism, mucosal injury drives ↑↑ production of galactose-deficient pIgA, which is not cleared by liver; the antibodies formed against pIgA are:
questions.exp: Anti glycan antibodies formed against pIgA → large immune complex. (Book p772)

questions.q: In the innocent bystander mechanism, the large IgA complex cannot cross the sinusoids into the liver parenchyma and is finally deposited in the mesangium.
opts: True — and the page adds that the misdirected filtration is into Bowman's space
True — hepatic vein, inferior vena cava, misdirected filtration at the glomerulus, mesangial deposit
False — Kupffer cells digest the complex before it reaches the inferior vena cava
False — the complex is deposited subepithelially rather than in the mesangium
questions.exp: Filtered at glomerulus (aqueous misdirected filtration) → deposited in mesangium. (Book p772)

questions.q: Fill up: The glomerular filtration of the IgA immune complex is labelled ______ filtration.
questions.exp: (Aqueous misdirected filtration). (Book p772)

questions.q: Match each condition with its m/c associated glomerular disease — 1) HIV 2) Cirrhosis (alcoholic & non alcoholic) 3) Hepatitis C … A) Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis B) Collapsing FSGS C) IgA nephropathy
questions.exp: HIV → collapsing FSGS; cirrhosis → IgA nephropathy; hepatitis C → MPGN. (Book p772)

questions.q: Match each condition with the glomerular lesion printed against it in the liver-disease block — 1) Hepatitis B 2) Hepatitis C 3) Cirrhosis … A) Membranous nephropathy B) MPGN pattern C) IgA nephropathy D) Minimal change disease
questions.exp: Hepatitis B → membranous nephropathy. (Book p772)

questions.q: Which pairing statement is TRUE per the m/c-associated-disease table?
opts: HIV is paired with membranous nephropathy in the same table
Hepatitis C is the infection paired with collapsing FSGS
Hepatitis B is the virus listed beside an MPGN pattern
Cirrhosis, alcoholic and non-alcoholic, pairs with IgA nephropathy
questions.exp: Cirrhosis → IgA nephropathy; HIV → collapsing FSGS; HBV → MN; HCV → MPGN. (Book p772)

questions.q: The sex preponderance written for IgA nephropathy presentation is:
questions.exp: Males > females. (Book p773)

questions.q: The >50% presentation cluster of IgA nephropathy is adolescents with synpharyngitic, episodic macrohematuria plus:
opts: Isolated oliguria with a normal urine sediment
questions.exp: Adolescents, synpharyngitic, episodic macrohematuria, intervening microhematuria + proteinuria. (Book p773)

questions.q: The asymptomatic arm with microhematuria and proteinuria covers what share of IgA patients?
questions.exp: 30-40% patients: asymptomatic + microhematuria and proteinuria. (Book p773)

questions.q: The 1% RPGN arm of IgA nephropathy is annotated as:
questions.exp: 1% patients: RPGN (adult HSP); 5% nephrotic; 5% directly as CKD. (Book p773)

questions.q: A 30-year-old has BP 160/100, proteinuria, creatinine 3.2 mg/dL and bilaterally contracted kidneys; biopsy shows mesangial IgA. Which printed arm of IgA nephropathy is this?
opts: The >50% adolescent cluster with intervening microhematuria and proteinuria
The 1% RPGN arm annotated as adult Henoch-Schonlein purpura
The 5% straight-to-CKD arm with a contracted kidney
questions.exp: As printed, the presentation list puts 5% directly into chronic kidney disease with hypertension, proteinuria, rising serum creatinine and a contracted kidney; the adolescent cluster with intervening microhematuria and proteinuria is the >50% arm, and crescentic disease is the 1% adult-HSP arm. (Book p773)

questions.q: The IgA prognosis rule of 1/3 splits into spontaneous resolution, develop CKD and:
opts: Near normal RFT with stable course
questions.exp: 1/3 spontaneous resolution; 1/3 near normal RFT, stable course; 1/3 develop CKD. (Book p773)

questions.q: In the MEST-C discussion, mesangial IgA alone carries normal features; the bad-prognosis indicators are IgA deposits outside mesangium (eg. capillary loops), any proliferation other than mesangial and:
opts: Tamm-Horsford protein casts within the tubules
Isolated C3 staining along the capillary loops
questions.exp: Bad prognosis: IgA outside mesangium; any non-mesangial proliferation; non IgA deposits (IgG, IgM). (Book p773)

questions.q: In the prognostic list on this page, crescents (the RPGN lesion) sit with the bad-prognosis findings.
opts: True — and gross hematuria is listed alongside them as a bad sign
True — crescents are grouped with the bad-prognosis entries
False — crescents are given no prognostic value at all
False — endocapillary hypercellularity is called chronic and inactive
questions.exp: Endocapillary hypercellularity → bad prognosis (active disease); segmental sclerosis + tubular atrophy → CKD → bad prognosis; crescents (RPGN) → bad prognosis. (Book p773)

questions.q: Among the 'others' prognostic notes, macrohematuria earns a good prognosis because it permits:
questions.exp: Macrohematuria: early diagnosis → good prognosis. (Book p773)

questions.q: Both serum complement levels and serum IgA are marked on this page as having no value in IgA nephropathy.
opts: True — but the note applies only to children
True — serum C3/C4 and serum IgA are each followed by 'no value'
False — serum IgA is the recommended screening test
False — a low C3 must be shown before biopsy is considered
questions.exp: Serum C3/C4 → no value; serum IgA → no value. (Book p773)

questions.q: IgA nephropathy investigations: light microscopy shows pure mesangioproliferative glomerulonephritis, while immunofluorescence shows:
opts: Subepithelial IgG spikes with a doubled membrane
Full house staining of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3 and C1q
Linear IgG along the glomerular basement membrane
questions.exp: IF: pIgA1 in mesangium ± C3 deposits. (Book p774)

questions.q: Conservative management targets: salt restriction <2 g Na+/day, protein 1 g/kg/day, BP control below:
questions.exp: Salt <2 g Na+/day; protein 1 g/kg/day; manage HTN (BP <140/90); ACE inhibitor/ARBs for proteinuria control. (Book p774)

questions.q: Steroid (short course oral) indications include proteinuria >1 g/day after 6 months of conservative management, nephrotic or RPGN (crescents) presentation, high E score and:
questions.exp: Indications end with: no significant CKD (if GFR ≤30/sclerosis/atrophy → no steroids). (Book p774)

questions.q: Steroids are withheld in IgA nephropathy when GFR falls at or below:
questions.exp: If GFR ≤30/sclerosis/atrophy → no steroids. (Book p774)

questions.q: Transplant in IgA nephropathy is indicated if CKD occurs, and the book notes what about recurrence post transplant?
questions.exp: Transplant: indication if CKD occurs; ↓ rate of recurrence post transplant. (Book p774)

questions.q: Match each complement pattern with its interpretation — 1) C3↓ and C4↓ 2) Transiently low C3 3) ↓C3 with normal C4 … A) eg. PSGN B) Classical complement pathway affected, eg. MPGN Type I C) Alternate complement pathway affected, eg. C3GN, adult HUS
questions.exp: C3↓+C4↓ classical (MPGN Type I); transiently low C3 eg. PSGN; ↓C3 normal C4 alternate (C3GN, adult HUS). (Book p774)

questions.q: IgA deposits are seen in IgA nephropathy, IgA-predominant PSGN (adult PSGN), full house effect (SLE) and light chain deposition disease, the last showing IgA & κ light chain deposit as part of:
questions.exp: Light chain deposition disease: IgA & κ light chain deposit (part of myeloma). (Book p774)

questions.q: All of the following carry IgA deposits per the note EXCEPT:
questions.exp: IgA deposits: IgA nephropathy, IgA-predominant PSGN, full house (SLE), light chain deposition disease; MN is not listed. (Book p774)

questions.q: Fill up: The full ______ effect, listed among IgA-deposit conditions, belongs to SLE.
questions.exp: Full house effect (SLE). (Book p774)

questions.q: Which steroid-indication statement is TRUE as per this page?
opts: Steroids are continued lifelong once started in IgA nephropathy
A GFR of 30 or below is itself a steroid indication
A high E score is an indication; GFR ≤30 or sclerosis/atrophy is not
Proteinuria >1 g/day at the first visit mandates steroids immediately
questions.exp: High E score (endocapillary cellularity) indicates steroid; GFR ≤30/sclerosis/atrophy → no steroids; proteinuria >1 g/day only after 6 months conservative. (Book p774)

questions.q: Fill up: In the conservative management of IgA nephropathy, proteinuria is controlled with ______ inhibitor/ARBs.
questions.exp: ACE inhibitor/ARBs for proteinuria control. (Book p774)

units.title: MPGN classification & etiology
units.guide: Mesangiocapillary eponym; the Type I vs Type II (C3 GN) table: IF patterns (IgG+IgM±C3 vs C3±IgG/M), 80% vs 100% transplant recurrence, 100% secondary banner, monoclonal (plasma cell dyscrasias, CLL) vs polyclonal causes (HCV/endocarditis/leprosy/P. malariae; VP shunt; SLE/Sjogren's/scleroderma; lipodystrophy + optic drusen), and EM deposit sites with dense-deposit eponym.

units.title: MPGN features, presentation, prognosis & IgA intro
units.guide: LM triad (capillary thickening, mesangial > endocapillary proliferation, lobular tuft ± uniform nodules) with figure label, 35/35/20/10 presentation split, 100% → CKD prognosis, HCV extrahepatic note (PCT, lichen planus, Sjogrens, cryoglobulinemia → non-thrombocytopenic palpable purpura), then IgA eponyms (Henoch-Schonlein/Berger's, m/c glomerular disease) and mIgA/pIgA biology.

units.title: IgA secondary causes & innocent bystander mechanism
units.guide: Mucosal injury list (coeliac, Whipple, tropical sprue, Crohns, UC; HIV → collapsing FSGS), cirrhosis clearance failure, spondyloarthritis examples with CD > UC, the innocent bystander chain (galactose-deficient pIgA → anti-glycan antibodies → large complex → hepatic vein → IVC → aqueous misdirected filtration → mesangial deposit), and the liver-disease/m/c-glomerular-disease table.

units.title: IgA presentation & prognosis
units.guide: Males > females; >50% adolescent synpharyngitic episodic macrohematuria with intervening microhematuria+proteinuria; 30-40% asymptomatic; 1% RPGN (adult HSP); 5% NS; 5% straight-to-CKD (HTN, ↑Cr, contracted kidney); rule of 1/3; MEST-C bad-prognosis set (extra-mesangial IgA, non-mesangial proliferation, non-IgA deposits, endocapillary hypercellularity, segmental sclerosis/tubular atrophy, crescents); macrohematuria good prognosis; C3/C4 and serum IgA no value.

units.title: IgA investigations & treatment ladder
units.guide: Pure mesangioproliferative LM and pIgA1 ± C3 IF; conservative targets (<2 g Na+/day, 1 g/kg/day protein, BP <140/90, ACEi/ARBs); short-course steroid indications (6-month >1 g/day, NS, RPGN crescents, high E score, no significant CKD; GFR ≤30 → none); transplant if CKD with ↓ recurrence.

units.title: Complement patterns & IgA-deposit conditions
units.guide: Complement tree (C3↓+C4↓ classical e.g. MPGN I; transiently low C3 e.g. PSGN; ↓C3 normal C4 alternate e.g. C3GN/adult HUS) and the IgA-deposit list (IgA nephropathy, IgA-predominant adult PSGN, full house SLE, light chain deposition disease IgA & κ part of myeloma).
